study.title: Acupuncture at KI3 in healthy volunteers induces specific cortical functional activity: an fMRI study
study.randomization: randomly divided into KI3 and non-acupoint groups according to a random-numbers table and random-numbers was in a sealed envelope
study.blinding: all volunteers were blind to the interventions they received; volunteers wore blindfolds during acupuncture
study.population: healthy college-student volunteers in Guangzhou, PRC
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) aged 21-28 years, (2) had never had acupuncture, (3) were eating well and not addicted to tobacco, tea, or coffee, (4) slept normally (before 0:00 am), (5) were moderate in size (BMI between 19 and 25), and (6) had no history of mental or nervous system diseases
study.exclusion_criteria: (7) had had no abnormal pain (including dysmenorrhea) or insomnia within in the month preceding the study, (8) no metal implants such as heart stents or metal teeth, (9) no skin diseases or skin damage at the acupoint, (10) did not have thrombocytopenia, hemophilia, or other blood coagulation-dysfunction diseases, and (11) were not claustrophobic. Further, 1 month before testing, we screened out volunteers who were predicted to have no response or oversensitive responses to acupuncture through the acupuncture-response prediction test

extraction_notes.note: Table 1 appears to have a labeling issue: the header rows for ALFF and REHO may be swapped based on the text description. The text states 'Increased ALFF was detected in the Left cerebrum frontal lobe medial frontal gyrus (BA10). Decreased ALFF was observed in the right parietal lobe and precuneus (BA7), left occipital lobe lingual gyrus (BA18)' but Table 1 lists BA7 and BA10 rows under ALFF, and BA7/BA10/BA18 rows under REHO. The extraction follows the table structure as printed, with the sign of peak intensity used to determine direction.
In Table 3, 'Right middle temporal gyrus' at BA39 has peak MNI coordinate X=-45, which corresponds to the left hemisphere. This inconsistency is preserved exactly as reported in the table.
In Table 4, the Z coordinate for 'Right middle occipital gyrus' (BA19) is listed as 12, whereas in Table 3 it is listed as -12. Both are transcribed exactly as reported in their respective tables.

No quantitative sensory/deqi data are reported (e.g., no VAS, NRS, MASS, or similar scale). The paper mentions 'The sensation data was calculated as covariate during the paired t-test' but provides no sensation scores or statistics.
No adverse events were reported in the paper. The paper does not explicitly state that there were no adverse events.
No expectancy or credibility measures were formally assessed or reported.
No clinical or behavioral outcome measures were reported. The study only assessed neuroimaging outcomes.

The sham acupuncture description is minimal: 'needles that did not pierce the skin at KI3.' No details about the specific sham device, visual appearance, or tactile sensation to the participant are provided.

The paper uses a within-arm crossover design for the KI3 group (sham then real acupuncture on the same day) without a washout period between conditions. This within-session carryover is not discussed as a limitation in the paper.

The between-group direct comparison (Table 4) methodology is described as 'direct comparison of the ALFF and ReHo changes between the KI3 and non-acupoint group' using REST1.8, but the specific statistical model (e.g., two-sample t-test, ANCOVA) is not explicitly stated.

The paper describes the ALFF sub-lobar result in Table 1 under the ALFF section with coordinates 18 0 0 and peak intensity 4.3743, cluster size 112. However, in the results text this region is described under 'REHO analysis' as 'Increased ReHo (T value was positive) was detected in the right sub-lobar, right medial frontal lobe (BA10).' There is an inconsistency between table headers and text descriptions. The extraction follows the table structure as printed.
extraction_notes.source_location: Table 1, page 6; results section ReHo analysis, page 6
